title: Active-slice criterion for operadic free extension
statement:
Use the universes and monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and presentability of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Use ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads and their inert maps as defined in [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability]. Let $u:\mathcal O\to\mathcal P$ be an inert-preserving map of small such operads. Let $\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be any monoidal infinity category; no presentability or cocompleteness is assumed. An algebra is a functor over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ preserving inert edges; their full functor infinity category is denoted $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal V)$. A base arrow is active if its opposite preserves the endpoints. Let $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{act}}$ be the wide subcategory of active arrows, and for $b\in\mathcal P_{[1]}$ put
$$K_b=\mathcal O_{\mathrm{act}}\times_{\mathcal P_{\mathrm{act}}}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{act}})_{/b}.$$
For an $\mathcal O$-algebra $A$, let $D_{A,b}:K_b\to\mathcal V$ send $(a,u(a)\to b)$, with $a$ over $[n]$ and successive inert colors $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, to $\bigotimes_{i=1}^n A(a_i)$, with value $\mathbf1$ for $n=0$; its arrows use the active algebra structure and composition of operations. Suppose, for every $A,b$, this diagram has a colimit and, for every pair of fixed objects $L,R\in\mathcal V$, the functor $x\mapsto L\otimes x\otimes R$ preserves this colimit. The tensor unit may be used for $L$ or $R$, so one-sided tensoring is included. Then restriction $u^*$ has a coherent left adjoint $u_!$, with
$$(u_!A)(b)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{K_b}D_{A,b},\qquad \operatorname{Map}(u_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(A,u^*B),$$
naturally in $A,B$. The adjunction unit is the cocone map associated to the identity operation of $u(a)$; the extension uses operadic substitution. All diagrams, colimits and adjunctions are homotopy coherent.

source.place: Proposition A.2.10 and Propositions A.4.3-A.4.4, Corollary A.4.5, printed pp.703,705-706, specialized to ordinary operads. The ordinary zero-fibers are contractible. The conditional criterion, rather than the unconditional presentably-monoidal theorem of the downstream free-extension node, is used here. Read from retained sandbox source; full shared archive WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.
Definitions 3.1.3, 3.1.13 and 3.1.17, printed pp.601,603-604; ordinary-operad specialization of the generalized inputs in Proposition A.4.4.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-generalized-active-extension-criterion] to the ordinary operads, the monoidal infinity category $\mathcal V^\otimes$, and the assumed colimits preserved by every two-sided tensoring functor. It supplies a coherent left adjoint $u_!$ to restriction, the objectwise formula $(u_!A)(b)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{K_b}D_{A,b}$, and the natural mapping-space equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(u_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(A,u^*B)$. Its identity-operation cocones give the stated unit, and its substitution construction gives the stated operadic operations and all higher coherences.

split_report.summary: Repaired the split by specializing the existing generalized active-extension criterion to ordinary nonsymmetric infinity operads. This removes the previous dependency cycle through def-coef-operadic-correspondence and lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability while retaining the exact active-slice colimit, unit, substitution, and coherent-adjunction conclusions.
split_report.blueprint: prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint.proof.md paragraph 2: supporting operadic foundation before the derived inverse limit; the two steps realize the ordinary specialization of the cited Gepner-Haugseng active-extension and coherent-adjunction argument.

tool_uses.why: The generic assertion that the core of a quasicategory is Kan verifies the ordinary zero-fiber hypothesis; no same-unit node supplies this quasicategory calculus.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N7-42823121a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: One commit with the item and its report only; no new nodes. Step 1 checked against the full statements of the four cited nodes. (1) The ordinary n=0 Segal condition makes O_[0] equivalent to a point; all its arrows are then equivalences, so it equals its core. That core is Kan by lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus, which is in unit sk-prop-sf-cbc; the declared tool use is accepted. So u_[0] is an equivalence. (2) I_n is the zigzag of n edges and n+1 vertices; singletons count as inert. Its limit is the stated homotopy pullback, and the vertex factors are contractible by the ordinary empty-product relative-limit clause. This reduces it to the ordinary product condition, and both sides are contractible at n=0. (3) The algebra definitions are identical. (4) O x_P (P_act)_{/b} = O_act x_{P_act} (P_act)_{/b} on all simplices, because u lies over the simplex category; D_{A,b} agrees, including the nullary unit. Step 2 uses only the statement of the same-unit node lem-coef-generalized-active-extension-criterion (unsplit). Its local two-sided tensor-preservation hypothesis is word for word the item's, and its conclusions cover the colimit formula, the Map equivalence, the identity-operation unit and substitution coherence. Edge cases checked: n=0,1, u=id, empty K_b, L or R equal to the unit, terminal V. My transitive-closure computation (535 nodes) shows no cycle; the earlier cycle through def-coef-operadic-correspondence is gone. Duplicate search covered the free-extension, cocomplete-extensions, free-cocone-criterion, active-slice-formula and active-lift nodes: the generalized criterion is a strict generalization, and citing it is sanctioned reuse. The item statement is unchanged and matches the shape of Lurie HA 3.1.3 in local form. I could not open the Gepner-Haugseng PDF: it is not archived and network access is blocked here. The proof takes nothing from it beyond the cited DAG node. No fixes.
